item.title: Stop putting women through brutal hysteroscopies without pain relief | Letters
item.summary: The medical system is biased against women, says Carole Kendall , pointing to the very different way men who have colonoscopies are treated I fully endorse everything Anna Moore writes in her excellent article on the lack of pain relief for hysteroscopies ( ‘It was barbaric. I was crying my eyes out’: why are so many women left in agony by routine womb examinations?, 16 August ). I have had three of these barbaric procedures, two of them being associated with being on hormone replacement therapy (HRT). All three were administered with very basic pain relief, ie a small amount of local anaesthetic, which I would compare to numbing a gum with a piece of ice and then proceeding with root canal treatment. I was offered a general anaesthetic on the third occasion, but this is way too much. At no point was anything else offered, like it is for colonoscopies. Continue reading...
